capabilities.directive: Blame rule for an error spike on service S starting at T. Candidates are deploys of S itself or S's direct depends_on services (not transitive, not dependents), status succeeded only, with T-30min <= at <= T inclusive. Culprit is the candidate with the latest at; if none, culprit_deploy_id is null. rollback is true only if a culprit exists and its kind is not config. Always returns exactly one document {culprit_deploy_id, rollback}.

versions.whenToUse: On-call asks which deploy most likely caused an error spike on a service at a given time, and whether to roll back.
versions.author: kap

capabilities.directive: Triage a failed CI run per fixtures/ci/RULES.md. failing_step = lowest-seq step with exit_code != 0. cause, first match wins using only that step: infra (exit_code 124/137/143 or log_tail contains, case-insensitive, OOMKilled / out of memory / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / Could not resolve host / No space left on device), flaky (a strictly earlier run of the same repo and commit, any branch, has a same-named step with exit_code 0), test (stage is test), else build. retry_safe = cause is infra or flaky.

$regexMatch.regex: OOMKilled|out of memory|ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|Could not resolve host|No space left on device

versions.whenToUse: A CI run failed and you need the failing step, the cause class (test|build|infra|flaky) and whether a plain retry is safe.

capabilities.directive: Given an advisory id, return which non-archived repos have at least one affected lockfile entry (exact package match, installed version within affected.min..affected.max inclusive, compared major then minor then patch numerically, direct and transitive alike), and which of those are patch fixable (every affected entry in the repo has the same major and minor as fixed_in; nothing is patch fixable when fixed_in is null). Returns exactly one document {affected_repos, patch_fixable}, both sorted ascending.

versions.whenToUse: A security advisory drops and you need to know which repos are affected and which can be fixed with a patch-level bump. Pass the advisory id, e.g. ADV-001.
